body:
Hi @kamilsk, I can reproduce the problem you described.

However, `amd64` is the right architecture for alpine linux. When I build GoReleaser locally, it is also possible to run it inside the alpine container.
```
$ pwd
/Users/jorin/go/src/github.com/goreleaser/goreleaser

$ goreleaser --snapshot

$ docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/dist/goreleaser_Linux_x86_64:/tmp golang:alpine /tmp/goreleaser --version
goreleaser version SNAPSHOT-cb179e040bd3d2b990fb0c39b1551ad7bdb27594, commit cb179e040bd3d2b990fb0c39b1551ad7bdb27594, built at 2017-05-10T07:41:42Z
```

I'm afraid this is an issue with the toolchain on Travis CI. Maybe it's related to the different cgo tooling.
We need to investigate further.


Travis:
```
$ go env
GOARCH="amd64"
GOBIN=""
GOEXE=""
GOHOSTARCH="amd64"
GOHOSTOS="linux"
GOOS="linux"
GOPATH="/home/travis/gopath"
GORACE=""
GOROOT="/home/travis/.gimme/versions/go1.8.1.linux.amd64"
GOTOOLDIR="/home/travis/.gimme/versions/go1.8.1.linux.amd64/pkg/tool/linux_amd64"
GCCGO="gccgo"
CC="gcc"
GOGCCFLAGS="-fPIC -m64 -pthread -fmessage-length=0 -fdebug-prefix-map=/tmp/go-build912071007=/tmp/go-build"
CXX="g++"
CGO_ENABLED="1"
PKG_CONFIG="pkg-config"
CGO_CFLAGS="-g -O2"
CGO_CPPFLAGS=""
CGO_CXXFLAGS="-g -O2"
CGO_FFLAGS="-g -O2"
CGO_LDFLAGS="-g -O2"
```

My laptop:
```
$ go env
GOARCH="amd64"
GOBIN=""
GOEXE=""
GOHOSTARCH="amd64"
GOHOSTOS="darwin"
GOOS="darwin"
GOPATH="/Users/jorin/go"
GORACE=""
GOROOT="/usr/local/Cellar/go/1.8.1/libexec"
GOTOOLDIR="/usr/local/Cellar/go/1.8.1/libexec/pkg/tool/darwin_amd64"
GCCGO="gccgo"
CC="clang"
GOGCCFLAGS="-fPIC -m64 -pthread -fno-caret-diagnostics -Qunused-arguments -fmessage-length=0 -fdebug-prefix-map=/var/folders/km/kqlfxy2j64dd_9gqb373c0hm0000gn/T/go-build192830200=/tmp/go-build -gno-record-gcc-switches -fno-common"
CXX="clang++"
CGO_ENABLED="1"
PKG_CONFIG="pkg-config"
CGO_CFLAGS="-g -O2"
CGO_CPPFLAGS=""
CGO_CXXFLAGS="-g -O2"
CGO_FFLAGS="-g -O2"
CGO_LDFLAGS="-g -O2"
```

> However, amd64 is the right architecture for alpine linux

Yes, sure

> When I build GoReleaser locally, it is also possible to run it inside the alpine container.

Could you provide `readelf -l <your local binary> | grep "program interpreter"` ?

As I said before

> The reason is that `/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2` doesn't exist at alpine linux.

but in your workflow (travis ci) it is used to build binary.
Related comment: https://github.com/gliderlabs/docker-alpine/issues/219#issuecomment-254741346

It is not critical for me, I can start using a build from sources instead of download binary.

issue.title: Use external, static linking.
issue.body:
Possible fix for #225 

I saw [Hugo](https://github.com/spf13/hugo/blob/master/goreleaser.yml#L4) uses this option and the Hugo release works on Alpine Linux.
But I don't think Hugo is release from Travis CI.
The only way to test this, is by making it part of a tag and let it run on Travis. 
Could also create a new repository to try this out.
But before trying this, @caarlos0, maybe you have any idea?

As this suggest there is some dynamic linking going on. Ideally, the binaries we produce from our Go programs are all static linked. See #226, maybe this can solve it. Have to try it out first though.

yes, it works!

```
docker run --rm \
-v "$(pwd)":/go/bin \
golang:latest \
go get github.com/goreleaser/goreleaser

docker run --rm -it \
-v "$(pwd)":/go/bin \
golang:alpine \
/bin/sh -c '/go/bin/goreleaser --version'

docker run --rm \
-v "$(pwd)":/go/bin \
golang:latest \
/bin/sh -c 'go get -d github.com/goreleaser/goreleaser && \
            cd /go/src/github.com/goreleaser/goreleaser && \
            go install --ldflags="-s -w -linkmode external -extldflags \"-static\"" .'

docker run --rm -it \
-v "$(pwd)":/go/bin \
golang:alpine \
/bin/sh -c '/go/bin/goreleaser --version'
```

Thanks a lot for you useful tool! :)
